_what: The Penpot colour pairs that check:contrast asserts. A FROZEN SNAPSHOT of board colours — the gate reads this file, not Penpot.
_why: check:contrast reads tokens.css and the app stylesheet, so it structurally CANNOT see a Penpot board. That is how SCRUM-93 happened: the 0e3 role chip sat at 2.77:1 on a signed-off board (EN and ZH) while every gate stayed green — despite SCRUM-45 having cleared 132 AA failures in this same file. A signed-off board is not a checked board. This file is the bridge: the pairs are extracted from Penpot by penpot-sweeps/penpot-contrast-sweep.js and frozen here so CI can assert them without a Penpot connection.
_limits: ⚠️ A snapshot is not a sweep. This asserts the pairs BELOW and nothing else — a NEW pair added to a board is invisible here until the sweep is re-run. Re-run the sweep after any Penpot colour change. The sweep also composites fillOpacity; this file stores the resolved backdrop, so a tint is recorded as the colour it actually renders as, never as its raw hex. ⚠️ AND — found the hard way on 2026-10-11 — that sweep asserted ONLY chip pairs (`role chip (label)` / `chip · `) until SCRUM-11 added a second branch for the League boards. The league parts are named `row 1 · Chen Family (bg)`, `row 1 · rank`, `divider · promotion line`, `art · tier badge label` — matching NEITHER pattern — so the whole League board would have stayed invisible to the file's only refresh mechanism, on the same shape of hole that let SCRUM-93 ship. AND FOUND 2026-10-12 (S56, SCRUM-114): the sweep filters BOARDS by name (/League/i), which is ASCII-only — so `ZH · 6b 联赛 / 第一周` has been invisible to the sweep entirely: the same shape of hole as the layer-pattern gap below, one level up. The 6c / 6d moment boards were named with `League` deliberately so they do not join it. ⚠️ AND THE LEAGUE ENTRIES ARE NOW KEYED BY THE PAIR, not by the board: the sweep dedupes on layer|fg|bg|threshold, so an EN/ZH twin (or the same component on 6, 6b and 6c) appears ONCE with a higher `shapes` count, and `board` names only the first producer. `shapes` is how many text shapes carry the pair — e.g. `art · tier badge label` reads 4 because all four league boards carry it, which is itself the evidence that ZH · 6b is no longer invisible. ⚠️ AND THE SCHEMA HERE IS TEXT-ONLY (`text` must be `normal` or `large`), so it structurally cannot carry the demoted card's NON-TEXT greys: the ghost badge outline and the level track are `--muted` #a39d92 at 0.35–0.5 opacity — **2.09 on the deep paper, 2.37 on plain paper**, below WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 for meaningful graphics. That is deliberate and reasoned, not missed: those greys are decorative and are NEVER the sole carrier of meaning (the captions at 4.50 and the → glyph carry it), and the landed/held badge outline is `--ink-soft` at 7.28:1. Recorded here because the alternative — an entry that cannot express its own requirement — is how a snapshot starts lying.
_refresh: node penpot-sweeps/penpot-contrast-sweep.js (via the Penpot MCP plugin) — it prints the pairs it measured and fails if any is below its minimum. ⚠️ SCRUM-11 extended it with the League branch (part 1b) and the top-level-board fix (trap 7). The thirteen League pairs below were measured from the LIVE board at revn 365 by exactly those rules, but the EXTENDED SCRIPT had not been run end-to-end when they were frozen (the Penpot plugin tab kept suspending). Before the next board colour change: run the sweep and diff its `league` array against these pairs. The SCRUM-114 pairs were measured by reading the new boards' shapes and recomputing the ratios with the sweep's own formula — the extended sweep itself has still not been run end-to-end (the plugin tab suspends). Run it and diff the `league` array before the next board colour change. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-12 (S56 · SCRUM-114): the LEAGUE half of the manifest (45 pairs, 8 boards) was measured LIVE at revn 369 by running part 1b verbatim against the file — not hand-computed. The transcription was then verified against a digest of the live sweep output (FNV-32 over the sorted canonical pair lines), so the frozen set is provably the measured set. ⚠️ The CHIP half (17 pairs) is still the older snapshot from parts 1 — it was not re-measured in this pass.
_source: Penpot file `JossPaperAR`, page "New-user tutorial · Core loop". The SCRUM-93 pairs were frozen from named version `S37b` at revn 287. The four SCRUM-94 pairs were measured live at revn 358 and saved as named version `S39 · SCRUM-94 — 0e8 disc + 7 Store Owned chip (revn 358)`; the six SCRUM-104 pairs (the confirm dialogs' cancel/no-thanks labels) were added at revn 364 under named version `S40 · SCRUM-104 — the 6 confirm dialogs grew 54px so Cancel sits ON the card`. All were saved via `penpot.currentFile.saveVersion()` — ⚠️ which EXISTS; the three-session-old claim that the plugin API had no version endpoint was itself the error (see follow-up-items.md), so do not repeat it. revn ticks on any change, including a live fault test that restores the same values. The thirteen SCRUM-11 pairs (the 6 / 6b League boards) were measured live at revn 365 — READ-ONLY, no board was touched, so there is no new named version and the file stayed at revn 365 throughout. The twenty-two SCRUM-114 pairs (the 6c / 6d moment boards, EN + ZH) were measured at **revn 367**, where those boards were CREATED — they are new surfaces drawn in the existing League language: the header, the tier badge and three rows are CLONES from the live league board, so the artwork is the board's own rather than a redraw. The new boards sit at x=5400. ⚠️ The 8 League boards scanned at revn 369 were EN · 6 League · ZH · 6 League / 联赛 · EN · 6b League / first week · ZH · 6b 联赛 / 第一周 · EN · 6c League / promotion moment · ZH · 6c League / 联赛 · 晋升时刻 · EN · 6d League / demoted · held · ZH · 6d League / 联赛 · 降级与留级 — the ZH · 6b board appearing in that list FOR THE FIRST TIME.
_rules: `text` must be `normal` (>=4.5:1) or `large` (>=3:1, i.e. >=24px, or >=18.66px bold). `min` is DERIVED from `text` by the gate and asserted equal to it — so the requirement cannot be quietly lowered to make a failing pair pass.
